findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.25, participial commentary, applied in reverse.
findings.diagnosis: 4.25 exists to remove trailing participles that append significance instead of stating a consequence, and the pass introduced one. The baseline states two things the earlier chapters argued, both as objects of argued, so both are claims the book has made and defended. Making the alignment problem civilizational asserts an entailment the sentence does not perform, and it demotes the second claim from something argued to something that follows. Therefore was the word carrying the relation, and it is the word that went.

findings.diagnosis: The retention limb applies. Philosophical is not a straw alternative here, it is what the previous five chapters were, and the sentence is the hinge where the book says it is now doing something else. The actual work of is the same move at the level of the noun: not the idea of building but the work. Both were removed, and the chapter's announcement of its own change in register went with them. Then before the question was also the second half of the if-then, and dropping it makes the conditional a loose sequence.

findings.diagnosis: But it exists is the turn after three concessions, uneven, contested, operating against significant headwinds, and it is the only positive claim in the paragraph. Deleting it leaves three concessions and an instruction. Both is also not a throwaway: the paragraph promises two different findings, one about what has been achieved and one about what has not, and the chapter delivers them in that order. Genuinely marks the second as a real opening rather than a rhetorical one.

regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. F1 is the first clear instance in this batch of the pass introducing a construction the catalog forbids rather than removing one. Compressing a coordinated that-clause into a trailing participle is the standard way a writer produces the shape 4.25 describes, and it happened here in the sentence stating the book's central thesis. The lesson generalizes: a compression that turns a second clause into a participle converts an argued claim into an asserted entailment, every time, and no word count records it.
